message.content:
### Your Rights as a Tenant in Texas (as of 2026) | Area | What You’re Entitled To | How to Exercise It | |------|------------------------|--------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • The landlord may hold a maximum of **one month’s rent** (or two if the lease is for a furnished unit).
• The deposit must be returned within **30 days** after you move out, minus any lawful deductions. | • Keep a copy of the lease and any move‑in inspection report.
• Request a written itemized statement of deductions. | | **Habitability** | • The landlord must keep the premises in a safe, livable condition (plumbing, heating, electrical, structural integrity, pest control, etc.). | • Notify the landlord in writing (email or certified mail) of any needed repairs.
• If the landlord fails to act, you may file a complaint with the Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs (TDHCA) or pursue a “repair‑and‑deduct” claim in small‑claims court. | | **Rent Payment** | • Rent is due on the date specified in the lease.
• Late fees are allowed only if the lease states them and they are reasonable (usually not more than 5% of the monthly rent). | • Keep receipts or bank records.
• If you’re late, notify the landlord and ask for a payment plan if needed. | | **Lease Termination** | • Either party may terminate a month‑to‑month lease with **30 days’ written notice**.
• For fixed‑term leases, the landlord must give you a written notice of termination at least **30 days** before the lease ends. | • Provide written notice (email or certified mail).
• Keep a copy of the notice and any acknowledgment from the landlord. | | **Privacy & Entry** | • Landlords must give **reasonable notice** (usually 24 hours) before entering, except in emergencies. | • Ask for a written notice of entry.
• If the landlord enters without notice, you can file a complaint or seek an injunction. | | **Discrimination** | • Texas law (and federal Fair Housing Act) prohibits discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income. | • Report any discriminatory actions to the Texas Commission on Human Rights (TCHR) or the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). | | **Maintenance of Records** | • Landlords must keep records of rent payments and maintenance requests. | • Request copies if needed for disputes or tax purposes. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlords must follow the Texas eviction procedure: serve a **Notice to Pay Rent or Quit** (10 days) or a **Notice to Vacate** (30 days) for non‑payment or lease violations.
• After the notice period, the landlord can file an unlawful detainer action in court. | • Respond to notices promptly.
• If you receive an eviction notice, you can file a counter‑claim or seek a stay of eviction in court. | | **Legal Remedies** | • Small‑claims court (up to $20,000) for disputes over rent, deposits, or damages.
• You can also file a civil action in district court for larger claims. | • Gather evidence (photos, receipts, correspondence).
• File the appropriate claim and attend the hearing. | | **Tenant’s Insurance** | • While not required by law, it’s wise to have renters insurance to cover personal property and liability. | • Shop for policies that cover theft, fire, water damage, and liability. | #### Quick Tips 1. **Document Everything** – Keep copies of the lease, receipts, emails, and any repair requests. 2. **Know the Notice Periods** – 24‑hour notice for entry, 30‑day notice for termination, 10‑day notice for non‑payment. 3. **Use Written Communication** – Email or certified mail provides a paper trail. 4. **Seek Legal Aid** – If you’re unsure, contact a local tenant advocacy group or legal aid office. #### Resources - **Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs (TDHCA)** – [tdhca.texas.gov](https://tdhca.texas.gov) - **Texas Commission on Human Rights (TCHR)** – [tchr.texas.gov](https://tchr.texas.gov) - **U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)** – [hud.gov](https://www.hud.gov) - **Texas Attorney General – Consumer Protection Division** – [attorneygeneral.texas.gov](https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov) If you have a specific situation (e.g., a dispute over a deposit, a notice of eviction, or a maintenance issue), let me know and I can give more tailored advice or help draft a letter.
